data.name: Bad Bots
data.detailed_description:
As Sam McRae, last surviving member of the “Titan Hauler” crew, you must hack and blast your way through an onslaught of truly bad 'bots to find a way to prevent a potential planet-destroying catastrophe. The mystery of what happened to everyone while you were in cryostasis unfolds around you as you wade through the bodies of your fallen shipmates, unloading round after round into your relentless automaton attackers.


  • Explore 170 danger-filled rooms throughout the ship including the Evacuation Bay, Mechanical Shafts and Robot Workshops while the rich sci-fi story unfolds in the Campaign Mode.
  • Engage in combat against more than 2000 deranged robots comprised of several unique types, all programmed to kill you.
  • Face off against 7 deadly bosses, each with distinctive attacks including the fire spewing Flamebot, electrified Orbs, the lethal grip of the Spider and Jack Hammer’s brutal pistons
  • Defend yourself with 8 robot bustin' weapons including your trusty Axe, Rifle, Shotgun, explosive Grenade Launcher, Pulsar Gun and more.
  • Try to survive 60 seconds against an endless onslaught of especially persistent and cranky gun-toting, knife wielding robots in 3 unique rooms in Challenge Mode.
  • Earn 14 challenging Achievements including “Run Amok,” “Top Dog” and “Reaper’s Friend.”
  • Enjoy full Controller and Steam Big Picture support so you can partake in all the ‘bot slayin’ goodness from the comforts of your couch.
Award-winning indie developer Vanni del Moral (Point Five Projects) has crafted an intense experience that pays homage to his gaming roots. Bad Bots is filled with 2D run-and-gun excitement coated in a bold visual style set in a large open space craft. Put your mettle to the metal in Bad Bots for both PC and Mac!

reviews.review:
FINALLY, SOME ROBOTS I CAN SHOOT WITHOUT FEELING BAD ABOUT IT! 

Bad Bots is actually fkng good! I booted this thing up expecting another crusty-A$$ indie game that looks like it escaped from a forgotten arcade cabinet, and instead I got a goddamn retro-style shooter that knows exactly what the fk it's doing. It's a 2D side-scrolling shooter. You shoot robots. You kill more robots. You save the world. The robots get turned into scrap metal. Everyone wins, except the robots, whose retirement plans have just been violently cancelled. WHAT MORE DO YOU FKING WANT?

The retro aesthetic hits that sweet nostalgia button without making the gameplay feel like it was assembled by a developer using a potato and three rusty nails. The graphics are excellent, the gameplay is solid, and the whole experience is ridiculously enjoyable. And here's the best part: IT ACTUALLY KNOWS HOW TO HAVE FUN. No bloated open world with 8,000 icons screaming for your attention. No NPC asking you to collect seventeen robot testicles to unlock a door. No endless bullSheet designed to inflate your playtime. Just you, your weapons, an army of murderous metal bastards, and enough shooting to make a robot factory file for bankruptcy. From the moment I started the campaign until the final moments, I was having a fkng blast. Time absolutely flies when you're busy committing industrial-scale robot genocide. I kept playing because I wanted to—not because some achievement was dangling a shiny digital carrot in front of my face like a manipulative little bastard. Bad Bots delivers exactly what it promises, and in an industry where games sometimes promise you the universe and deliver a damp sandwich, that deserves some fkng respect. 

FINAL VERDICT: A fantastic little retro shooter that punches well above its weight. If you enjoy old-school side-scrolling action, give this magnificent ba$tard a chance. Buy it. Play it. Shoot some robots. Save the world. And remember: the only good bot is a bot that explodes dramatically on screen.
